name: CA-33
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Aguilar's large financial advantage ($4.7M raised, $3.5M on hand)
No serious outside spending against Aguilar
Markets price Aguilar at ~95% to win
model.rationale: Aguilar holds a well-funded incumbency in a district that leans Democratic by seven points, with no outside opposition spending and prediction markets pricing his win probability around 95%. With no polls or expert ratings available, the fundamentals-based margin of roughly 20 points stands as the best estimate.
model.watch: Any late polling or unexpected outside spending against Aguilar would be the first sign the race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Pete Aguilar, the Democratic incumbent, seeks another term in a Southern California district that voted about seven points more Democratic than the nation in recent cycles. He enters the general election with a commanding financial position, having raised nearly $4.7 million and holding $3.5 million on hand, while Republican challenger Stephanie Vargas reports no significant fundraising. No outside groups have spent against Aguilar.

With no public polling and no expert ratings tracking the race, the outlook rests on the district's lean, Aguilar's incumbency advantage, and his money edge, all pointing to a comfortable Democratic win. Prediction markets agree, pricing Aguilar's chances at roughly 95 percent.
